text:
Predicates:
Salads(x) ::: x eats salads regularly.
HealthConscious(x) ::: x is very conscious about their health and eating habits.
HealthConsciousChildhood(x) ::: x grew up in a health-conscious childhood home.
NutritionalIntakes(x) ::: x fulfills their nutritional daily intakes.
GoodRelationship(x) ::: x has good relationships with their parents.
Gym(x) ::: x visit the gym at least once a day.
Premises:
∀x (Salads(x) → HealthConscious(x)) ::: All people who eat salads regularly are very conscious about their health and eating habits.
∀x (HealthConsciousChildhood(x) → Salads(x)) ::: All people who grew up in health-conscious childhood homes eat salads regularly.
∀x (NutritionalIntakes(x) → HealthConsciousChildhood(x)) ::: All people who fulfill their nutritional daily intakes grew up in health-conscious childhood homes.
∀x (GoodRelationship(x) → NutritionalIntakes(x)) ::: If people have good relationships with their parents, then they fulfill their nutritional daily intakes.
∀x (GoodRelationship(x) → ¬Salads(x)) ::: If people have good relationships with their parents, then they do not eat salads regularly.
∀x (Gym(x) → NutritionalIntakes(x)) ::: If people visit the gym at least once a day, then they always fulfill their daily nutritional intakes.
(HealthConsciousChildhood(taylor) ∧ GoodRelationship(taylor)) ⊕ (¬HealthConsciousChildhood(taylor) ∧ ¬GoodRelationship(taylor)) ::: It is either both true that Taylor grew up in a health-conscious childhood home and she has a good relationship with her parents, or it is true that Taylor neither grew up in a health-conscious childhood home nor has a good relationship with her parents.
Conclusion:
Salads(taylor) ::: Taylor eats salads regularly.
